item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":47,"end_unit":48,"fact_summary":"In 2023, BAMF maintained interpreter-quality safeguards requiring training, C1 German proficiency, adherence to standards including accuracy, impartiality, integrity, and confidentiality, and a complaint process that could terminate interpreter contracts. However, no 2023 complaint data were available, and earlier interpreter misconduct decisions had not triggered reassessment of affected cases.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The standards were current in April 2023, while some cited complaint and misconduct figures predated 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These were federal administrative safeguards operating under the Scholz government; the source does not identify Olaf Scholz as personally directing them.","limitations":["No evidence is provided about Scholz's personal involvement, funding decisions, or review of the safeguards.","The report does not quantify 2023 enforcement outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":49,"end_unit":51,"fact_summary":"Germany's 2022 Act on the acceleration of asylum court proceedings and asylum procedures took effect on 1 January 2023, permitting courts in specified cases to dispense with personal hearings and changing bias-motion procedure; average asylum appeal processing time was 21.3 months through 31 August 2023, down from 26 months in 2022, while 120,247 cases remained pending in October 2023 and observers attributed continuing capacity problems to understaffing.","question_ids":["4B.4","6B.2","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legislative change applied throughout 2023; the performance figures cover the stated 2023 cutoffs.","ruler_attribution":"The reform was enacted by the federal legislature under the Scholz coalition government; the source does not establish personal authorship by Scholz.","limitations":["The report says the 2023 decline could not yet be attributed to the reform because most concluded cases began earlier.","No direct evidence links Scholz personally to staffing or court-capacity decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":54,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"From 1 January 2023, statutory counselling covered the whole asylum procedure through final appeal, but asylum seekers still generally lacked systematic free legal representation at the BAMF first-instance stage; rural applicants could face long travel distances to specialist advice.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.3","4B.7","6B.2","6B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The expanded counselling rule applied from 1 January 2023; the access limitations were reported for the 2023 update.","ruler_attribution":"This was a federal legal and administrative framework in force under the Scholz government; personal attribution to Scholz is not established.","limitations":["The source does not provide national uptake or outcome data for counselling.","It does not show whether Scholz personally proposed or monitored the reform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":55,"end_unit":58,"fact_summary":"In 2023 Germany sent 74,622 outgoing Dublin requests, received 55,728 acceptances, and carried out 5,053 transfers; it received 15,568 incoming requests and carried out 4,275 transfers to Germany. Between January and August, Germany applied the sovereignty clause in 574 cases, taking responsibility for asylum procedures itself.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.7","3B.7","6B.6","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The figures cover 2023, with the sovereignty-clause figure covering January-August.","ruler_attribution":"These were federal implementation outcomes of Germany's Dublin policy under the Scholz government, administered principally by BAMF and the Länder.","limitations":["The source does not establish Scholz's personal role in individual transfers or operational decisions.","The figures do not by themselves show whether transfers complied with all human-rights safeguards."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":60,"end_unit":62,"fact_summary":"In 2023, 2,065 cases of church asylum connected to Dublin procedures were reported to BAMF, and between January and September Germany became responsible for asylum applications in 1,676 cases. The year also saw reported breaches of church asylum involving police entry and attempted apprehensions in Viersen and Schwerin; one transfer was stopped after protests and intervention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The case counts and incidents occurred during 2023, with the responsibility figure limited to January-September.","ruler_attribution":"The incidents involved federal and subnational authorities under the Scholz-era legal framework; the source does not attribute the operational orders personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The report gives no finding that Scholz ordered or approved the specific police actions.","The 1,676 figure cannot be shown to result directly from church asylum in every case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":62,"end_unit":65,"fact_summary":"During the first half of 2023, 47 Dublin transfers involved police use of physical restraints. Dublin appeals had to be filed within one week without automatic suspensive effect, and the report states that this deadline was often practically difficult to meet because applicants lacked timely legal assistance; courts nevertheless had to suspend transfer pending a request for interim relief.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","6B.2","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The restraint figure covers the first half of 2023; the procedural rules were in force during the period.","ruler_attribution":"These were statutory and administrative practices under the federal government, implemented by police, BAMF, and courts; personal responsibility of Scholz is not demonstrated.","limitations":["The source does not specify whether the restraints were lawful or excessive in each of the 47 cases.","The legal-assistance assessment is reported as a practical concern, not a court finding applicable to every case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":72,"end_unit":76,"fact_summary":"Between January and October 2023 BAMF recorded 55,368 inadmissibility or other non-substantive case dispositions, including 29,398 based on the Dublin Regulation and 10,207 subsequent applications. For applicants already protected in Greece, BAMF decided 16,495 applications in 2023: 5,185 refugee-status grants, 3,596 subsidiary-protection grants, 3,510 removal bans, 2,299 merits rejections, and 1,905 formal decisions.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.4","6B.2","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The inadmissibility figures cover January-October 2023; the Greece-related decisions are reported for 2023, with some source notes indicating partial-year underlying parliamentary data.","ruler_attribution":"These were BAMF decisions under federal asylum policy during Scholz's chancellorship; the source does not identify Scholz as personally deciding cases.","limitations":["The report cautions that some 2023 source statistics have differing cutoff dates.","Aggregate outcomes cannot establish fairness or quality in individual cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":78,"end_unit":83,"fact_summary":"Germany initiated 200 airport asylum procedures in the first half of 2023. The airport procedure imposed a two-day BAMF decision window and a three-day court deadline for interim relief; 29.5% of cases were rejected as manifestly unfounded in the first half of 2023. The report states that airport procedures had been criticized for higher rejection rates, limited outside contact, tight deadlines, and inadequate vulnerability screening; two 2023 cases involving removal to Iran were publicly reported despite a federal removal ban for Iran.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.7","3B.4","4B.3","4B.7","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The volume and rejection figures cover the first half of 2023; the reported cases and legal framework were current during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The airport procedure was a federal statutory and BAMF-administered system under the Scholz government; the source does not show that Scholz personally directed the cases or removals.","limitations":["The report notes that applicant profiles may partly explain higher rejection rates.","The two reported removals are described as refusals of entry by the ministry, while the human-rights concerns remain contested in the cited accounts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":84,"end_unit":87,"fact_summary":"Airport asylum interviews involved an initial Federal Police interview followed by a BAMF interview, often under severe time pressure. The report records concerns about lengthy questioning, inconsistent mandates and qualifications, telephone interpretation, inadequate interpreters, and interviews conducted in languages applicants did not understand. In the first half of 2023, 54 appeals against airport decisions were lodged, with 3 granted and 44 rejected.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","4B.3","4B.4","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The appeal figures cover the first half of 2023; several interview-quality observations are based on practitioner evidence from earlier years but describe the continuing procedure.","ruler_attribution":"The procedures were operated by federal police and BAMF under the federal government; the source does not establish personal direction by Scholz.","limitations":["Some interview-quality evidence predates 2023 and is presented as continuing concern rather than a 2023 audit.","Appeal outcomes may concern applications lodged in earlier years."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is an asylum-procedure country report and contains little direct evidence about Olaf Scholz's personal decisions, statements, appointments, integrity, economic policy, foreign policy, nuclear risk, or overall period-end outcomes.","Facts are attributed to the federal government, legislature, BAMF, police, courts, and Länder only where the source supports institutional attribution; no personal score or causal judgment about Scholz is made."]}
